description: We are AstroPulse Nexus, a team passionate about space exploration, artificial intelligence, and healthcare innovation. Our goal is to develop an intelligent health monitoring solution for astronauts during space missions using AI, data analysis, and software technologies. We welcome motivated students, developers, designers, and researchers who want to collaborate, share ideas, and build something meaningful for the future of space exploration. Let's innovate together!
summary: Astroval is an Earth-independent astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision-support platform designed for deep-space exploration. Because communication latencies of up to 44 minutes round-trip between Mars and Earth make real-time telemedicine impossible, crews require autonomous onboard medical intelligence. Astroval integrates continuous biometric telemetry, cabin Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) metrics, an interactive anatomical systems map, a Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-60) cognitive assessment, and an Edge-AI Flight Surgeon advisor. Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) payloads—including the Bio-Monitor smart garment, Radi-N2 neutron dosimeters, and Vascular Echo—Astroval detects early physiological anomalies such as Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone demineralization, and circadian fatigue, prescribing immediate countermeasures while securely queuing encrypted data for Deep Space Network (DSN) transmission.
details:
Project Details

What It Does & How It Works Astroval functions as an onboard Mission Medical Command Center that operates autonomously without requiring real-time ground control connectivity. The platform features five core modules:

  1. Executive Biometrics & Anatomical Body Map: Tracks heart rate, HRV, SpO2, core temperature, cumulative radiation dose (mSv), sleep score, and fatigue index across four crew profiles. Crew members can click interactive anatomical nodes (Cardiovascular, Musculoskeletal, Neurological/Ocular SANS, Immune, and Behavioral) to inspect targeted telemetry and prescribed countermeasures.
  2. Edge-AI Flight Surgeon Advisor: Uses a large language model integrated with live astronaut vitals and cabin CO2 levels to generate instant, personalized space-medicine diagnostics and preventive tips without waiting for Earth-to-Mars signal round-trips.
  3. NASA 5 Hazards & CSA Research Matrix: Maps real-time mission parameters directly against NASA’s RIDGE framework (Radiation, Isolation, Distance from Earth, Altered Gravity, and Hostile Closed Environments) alongside CSA life-science technologies (Radi-N2 bubble detectors, Bio-Monitor smart shirt, and Vascular Echo).
  4. Cognitive Vigilance (PVT-60) & Behavioral Logging: Includes an interactive millisecond-precision Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-60) to detect circadian fatigue prior to critical EVA or robotic operations, paired with an encrypted daily stress and sleep self-evaluation log.
  5. Countermeasure Engine & DSN Store-and-Forward Sync: Tracks daily execution of ARED high-torque resistance workouts, Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) sessions, and 460nm circadian blue-light therapy, while packaging telemetry with AES-256 encryption for Deep Space Network (DSN) passes.

Benefits & Intended Impact Astroval bridges the telemedicine gap for Artemis lunar missions and future Mars transits by empowering crews to detect and mitigate physiological degradation early. Furthermore, by tracking accelerated microgravity-induced bone resorption and arterial stiffening, the platform supports translational research that improves osteoporosis, cardiovascular, and aging treatments on Earth.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & UI: React (JSX), JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Lucide-React icons
  • AI & Decision Support: Google Gemini API (gemini-3-flash-preview) with structured JSON clinical outputs and offline heuristic fallback
  • Presentation & Prototyping: HTML5/CSS3 responsive slide deck architecture

Creativity & Design Considerations We designed Astroval with a high-contrast, low-glare dark interface optimized for spacecraft cabin lighting, non-blocking toast alerts that never interrupt critical workflows, offline-first resilience, and strict adherence to NASA/CSA scientific terminology without using any unauthorized NASA logos or mission insignia.
